nodes.name: Seed-mediated growth of Au CCs and BNPs
nodes.procedure: The syntheses of gold CCs and gold BNPs have been reported previously using seed-mediated growth in aqueous solutions of cationic surfactants.
nodes.source_text: All shape-specific gold and palladium nanoparticles used in this work (Supplementary Fig. 1) were synthesized using seed-mediated growth in aqueous solutions of cationic surfactants21–23

nodes.name: Seed-mediated growth of Pd BNPs
nodes.procedure: The syntheses of palladium BNPs have been reported previously using seed-mediated growth in aqueous solutions of cationic surfactants.
nodes.source_text: All shape-specific gold and palladium nanoparticles used in this work (Supplementary Fig. 1) were synthesized using seed-mediated growth in aqueous solutions of cationic surfactants21–23

nodes.name: Adapted synthesis of Pd CCs
nodes.procedure: The synthesis of palladium CCs was derived from the method for gold CCs synthesis by replacing the HAuCl₄ with Na₂PdCl₄ in the growth solution.
nodes.source_text: The synthesis of palladium CCs was derived from the method for gold CCs synthesis by replacing the HAuCl₄ with Na₂PdCl₄ in the growth solution.

nodes.name: Electrode preparation by drop-casting
nodes.procedure: All electrodes were prepared by drop-casting a concentrated gold or palladium nanoparticle solution onto the gold or palladium foil substrate, respectively. All prepared electrodes were dried, washed with methanol and water to clean their surface from the surfactants used in the nanoparticle synthesis, and then used as prepared or stored under argon.

nodes.description: Lead UPD surface characterization before/after CO2RR

surface_characterization.value: rich in {100} and {111} terraces before, shifted to dominant {111} after 120 min CO2RR

nodes.source_text: The lead UPD voltammogram revealed that the initial gold CCs were rich in {100} and {111} terraces... After two hours of CO2RR electrolysis at -0.6 V versus RHE, the lead UPD voltammogram revealed the dominance of {111} terraces

nodes.characterization_summary: Gold BNPs preserved overall structure with minor current density decay but showed sintering between BNPs and with substrate after 300 min CO2RR at -0.6 V vs RHE; slight surface smoothening observed on external arms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: While gold BNPs generally preserved their overall structure and showed minor decay in current density over time... after five hours of electrolysis we observed structural changes (Fig. 1a–h), with pronounced sintering between a BNP and the substrate (Fig. 1g,h) and between multiple BNPs (Fig. 1f,d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Lead UPD on gold BNPs shows initial surface rich in {110} and {111} terraces with broad peaks from steps/kinks; after 120 min CO2RR at -0.6 V vs RHE, {111} and {110} features remain dominant, become more pronounced with minor peak shift indicating surface restructuring.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lead UPD voltammogram of gold BNPs before electrolysis shows that the initial surface was rich in {110} and {111} terraces, with broad peaks consistent with the presence of steps and kinks associated with the nanoscale surface curvature. After two hours of CO2RR electrolysis at −0.6 V versus RHE, {111} and {110} UPD features remained dominant and became more pronounced, and a minor shift in the peaks was observed, suggesting that some surface restructuring took place.

nodes.characterization_summary: Gold CCs show breakage of structural integrity and sintering after 60-300 min CO2RR at -0.6 V vs RHE; individual CCs also degrade while touching CCs exhibit interface sintering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Already after one hour of electrolysis under CO2RR conditions at −0.6 V versus RHE, a breakage of the structural integrity of the CC walls facing the electrolyte and a sintering of the adjacent CCs could be seen... We found that individual CCs still underwent some structural degradation, while CCs that were touching each other exhibited sintering at the interface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lead UPD on gold CCs shows initial {100} and {111} terraces rich surface with high-index shoulder peak; after 120 min CO2RR at -0.6 V vs RHE, {111} terraces become dominant indicating change in crystallographic surface structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lead UPD voltammogram revealed that the initial gold CCs were rich in {100} and {111} terraces, with the leftmost shoulder peak in the voltammogram associated with the presence of high-index surfaces. After two hours of CO2RR electrolysis at −0.6 V versus RHE, the lead UPD voltammogram revealed the dominance of {111} terraces in the resultant structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Gold CCs show less pronounced disfigurement and sintering under HER conditions compared to CO2RR after 120 min at -0.6 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The disfigurement and sintering of the CC structures along with a drop in the current density, Jgeom, were more pronounced under CO2RR than under HER conditions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Palladium CCs show no noticeable structural transformation or interparticle sintering after 300 min CO2RR at -1.2 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast to gold CCs, palladium CCs did not undergo noticeable structural transformation or interparticle sintering even after five hours of electrolysis at −1.2 V versus RHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: Palladium BNPs preserve overall shape after 300 min CO2RR at -1.2 V vs RHE, with minor dulling of sharp tips.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Similarly, palladium BNPs preserved their overall shape after five hours of CO2RR electrolysis under the same conditions, although some minor dulling of the sharp BNP tips was observed.
